thread_analysis.thread_summary: Fulltech (Haudi brand) SIG membership registration support. Two administrative issues: (1) The URL in Allion's SIG member registration guide PDF now redirects away from the expected page — the SIG portal changed so the description page no longer exists, and the flow goes directly to 'Begin Application'. (2) The customer's domain is fulltech1963.com (not .jp), so the guide's reference to a JP Whois certificate does not apply — a Whois certificate for the .com domain was attached and accepted as domain ownership proof. Short thread, quick resolution.
all_questions_found: SIG member registration guide URL is invalid — where to proceed?
Non-JP domain: what proves domain ownership for SIG member registration?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: SIG portal URLs change over time and documentation can become stale. The member registration flow no longer includes an intermediate description page — customers should navigate directly to 'Begin Application'. For domain ownership verification, the SIG accepts Whois certificates for non-JP domains. A standard Whois PDF printout from any Whois provider is sufficient.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Keep guides updated as SIG portal evolves. For non-JP domain customers, Whois certificate substitutes for the JP domain-specific proof referenced in standard guides.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Outdated guides cause customer confusion and may lead to incomplete applications. Missing domain ownership documentation prevents SIG account creation and delays the entire qualification timeline.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified. Allion proactively attached the Whois certificate and guided the customer through the updated portal flow.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Periodically verify that SIG member registration guide URLs remain valid — the SIG portal is updated without advance notice. Maintain a non-JP domain checklist item: 'Whois certificate required for .com, .net, and other non-JP domains.'
